translation: Asaidula (refrain), an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana! Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!

Our cries of hunger are the calls of Telangana; until the state is won, these tiger roars will not stop now. Our cries of hunger are the calls of Telangana; until the state is won, these tiger roars will not stop now.
(Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!)

Joined as allies in struggle, red eyes turned into crowbars, a wrathful torrent, becoming forces that crush their schemes; joined as allies in struggle, red eyes turned into crowbars, a wrathful torrent, becoming forces that crush their schemes. Look at the grief in the gutted doorways, brother; look at the sobbing villages and stir the fury in your heart.
(Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!)

How long must we keep enduring? To win agreement on a clean break, only if we dare anything, whatever it takes, will there be Telangana. How long must we keep enduring? To win agreement on a clean break, only if we dare anything, whatever it takes, will there be Telangana. O Andhra colonisers, you will be driven out and buried! Village after village is ablaze, a festival of Telangana!
(Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!)

Domination, arrogance, real-estate land grabs; who is the Andhra man to rule over us? Let us drive him out and rule ourselves. Domination, arrogance, real-estate land grabs; who is the Andhra man to rule over us? Let us drive him out and rule ourselves. The neither-this-nor-that fence-sitters, the United Andhra backers, the political leaders are frogs sitting in pond scum.
(Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!)

Under a rule of discrimination, life was made wretched; all our resources were carried away, and it became oppression and plunder. Under a rule of discrimination, life was made wretched; all our resources were carried away, and it became oppression and plunder. The tears of the wounded heart become a war march, little brother; smouldering and smouldering, Telangana is boiling over, little brother.
(Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!)

We are the ones who learned to raise our fists, who hurled spears and charged, who chased out the Nizams, who brought the Nazis to their knees. We are the ones who learned to raise our fists, who hurled spears and charged, who chased out the Nizams, who brought the Nazis to their knees. An outsider's code of justice will not get us far, brother; if the division does not happen, something drastic will happen, brother.
(Asaidula, an aarti! The thrill of anklet bells on our feet! The courage marching out to the battle for Telangana!)
summaryEn:
Asaidula Haarati is a protest song from the movement for a separate Telangana state. It opens with festive imagery, an aarti, the jingle of anklet bells and the sung cry 'Asaidula', and turns it into the 'himmat' (courage) of people marching to the Telangana 'ladai' (fight), mixing Telugu with the Urdu-derived words common in Telangana speech. The singer addresses fellow Telanganites as 'brother', declaring that their cries of hunger are the call for statehood and that these 'tiger roars' will not stop until the state is won.

The verses pile up grievances: discriminatory rule, resources carried away, oppression, plunder and real-estate land grabs by those the song calls Andhra 'colonisers'. It mocks fence-sitters, supporters of a united Andhra (Samaikyandhra) and politicians as frogs in pond scum. The final verse calls on a memory of resistance, people who raised their fists, hurled spears and drove out the Nizams, to warn that drastic consequences will follow if the division does not happen. In form, each verse sings its opening couplet twice before a new closing couplet, and the bracketed refrain returns after every verse, which makes the song well suited to rallies and group singing.

అసైదులా హారతి తెలంగాణ ప్రత్యేక రాష్ట్ర ఉద్యమానికి చెందిన ఒక నిరసన పాట. హారతి, కాళ్ల గజ్జల సందడి, 'అసైదులా' అనే కూత వంటి పండుగ వాతావరణంతో మొదలై, దాన్ని తెలంగాణ లడాయికి కదులుతున్న ప్రజల హిమ్మతిగా మారుస్తుంది. తెలంగాణ మాటల్లో కలిసిపోయిన లడాయి, హిమ్మతి, గమ్మతి వంటి ఉర్దూ పదాలు పాటకు ప్రత్యేకమైన రంగును ఇస్తాయి. గాయకుడు తోటి తెలంగాణ వాసులను 'తమ్ముడా' అని పిలుస్తూ, మా ఆకలి కేకలే తెలంగాణ పిలుపులని, రాష్ట్రం వచ్చేదాకా ఈ పులి కేకలు ఆగవని ప్రకటిస్తాడు.

చరణాలలో వివక్షతో కూడిన పాలన, తరలిపోయిన వనరులు, అణచివేత, దోపిడీ, రియల్ ఎస్టేట్ కబ్జాలు వంటి ఆవేదనలను ఒకదాని తర్వాత ఒకటిగా చెబుతూ, ఆంధ్ర వలసవాదులను ఎల్లగొట్టాలని పిలుపునిస్తుంది. అటు ఇటు కాని వారిని, సమైక్యాంధ్రవాదులను, రాజకీయ నేతలను నాచులో కూర్చున్న కప్పలతో పోల్చి ఎద్దేవా చేస్తుంది. చివరి చరణం పిడికిలెత్తిన, బరిసెలు విసిరిన, నైజాములను తరిమిన పోరాట జ్ఞాపకాన్ని గుర్తుచేస్తూ, పంపకం జరగకపోతే తీవ్ర పరిణామాలు తప్పవని హెచ్చరిస్తుంది. ప్రతి చరణంలో మొదటి రెండు పాదాలు రెండుసార్లు పాడి, తర్వాత కొత్త ముగింపు పాదాలు వస్తాయి; ప్రతి చరణం తర్వాత పల్లవి మళ్ళీ రావడం వల్ల ఈ పాట సభల్లో, ఊరేగింపుల్లో అందరూ కలిసి పాడుకోవడానికి అనువుగా ఉంటుంది.
